node_title: Modeling Membrane Degradation in PEM Electrolyzers with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
summary: Root node. Hybrid physics + ML study introducing the first PINN for PEM-electrolyzer membrane degradation, coupling a membrane-thinning ODE with a cell-voltage ODE to jointly forecast degradation and infer physical parameters from sparse noisy data.

Motivates PEM electrolyzers for sustainable hydrogen and frames membrane degradation as the key reliability/safety bottleneck; contrasts interpretable-but-parameter-heavy physics models with flexible-but-inconsistent data-driven models, motivating a PINN hybrid.
Describes the electrochemical reactions and the cell-voltage decomposition (open-circuit, activation, and ohmic overpotentials) that govern PEM electrolyzer operation.
Explains the chemical degradation pathway (free-radical formation) and the membrane-thinning mechanism that raises ohmic resistance and shifts cell voltage over time.
Provides the PINN background: a loss function combining a data-fit term with physics-residual terms that enforce the governing ODEs, enabling physically consistent learning from limited data.
Lays out the methodology: data generation, the coupled governing equations, and the PINN configuration for joint forecasting and parameter inference.
Describes the synthetic degradation trajectories and the sampling of ~100 noisy points used to train the model.
States the two coupled ODEs - first-order membrane-thinning law and the cell-voltage evolution under degradation - that form the physics residuals.

node_title: 5.3 Setup for the Joint Forecasting and Parameter Inference Using PINNs
summary: Defines the network architecture (2 hidden layers, 10 and 5 neurons, sigmoid, Adam lr=0.005, up to 7,500 epochs) and the joint forecasting + parameter-inference training scheme.
node_path: 5.3 Setup for the Joint Forecasting and Parameter Inference Using PINNs

summary: Reports that the PINN recovers the degradation constant (k5 ~ 1.01 vs 1.0), achieves low test RMSE (voltage 0.0047, thickness 6.1e-5), and extrapolates across ~66% of the cycle from the first third; outperforms a conventional ANN.
Summarizes the PINN as a data-efficient, physically interpretable tool for membrane-degradation diagnostics and outlines future work toward real-operational-data validation.
Tabulates the physical and electrochemical constants used in the governing equations.
Lists the free-radical reaction set underlying the chemical membrane-degradation pathway.
